prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core pitch
- Claim recent economic stabilisation (lower inflation, rising real wages, growth) is due to the Conservative plan; argue Labour would risk higher taxes, borrowing and weaker border/defence.
- Offer a “secure future” built on lower taxes, controlled migration, strong defence, better public services, support for families and communities.

Tax, work and business
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises in income tax or VAT.
- Triple Lock Plus: state pension and pensioner tax‑free allowance both rise by the highest of earnings, prices or 2.5%; retain pension tax reliefs and benefits.
- Childcare: 30 free hours from 9 months to school start by Sept 2025; expand wraparound care.
- Child Benefit: move to household assessment; taper between £120k–£160k combined income.
- Pro‑business: retain full expensing (aim to extend to leasing), no rise in corporation tax; SME 10‑point plan (rates relief, finance access, prompt payment, cut reporting burdens).
- Infrastructure: redeploy £36bn HS2 savings to regional transport; expand gigabit and 5G; rail and road upgrades; support EV charging and SAF.

Welfare and skills
- Tighten disability and fit‑note assessments; expand mental‑health support; tougher sanctions for long‑term unemployed; fraud bill; complete Universal Credit roll‑out.
- Education: mobile‑phone bans in school; protect day‑to‑day funding per pupil; expand teacher incentives; mandate 2 hours PE weekly; Advanced British Standard replaces A/T levels split.
- 100,000 extra apprenticeships funded by closing low‑outcome degrees; Lifelong Learning Entitlement.
- Mandatory National Service at 18: 12 months military/cyber (paid, competitive) or part‑time civic service.

Health and social care
- NHS spending to rise above inflation; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgeries upgraded; 50 more diagnostic centres.
- £3.4bn tech plan (NHS App as single front door, AI diagnostics, data platform); cut management by 5,500.
- Dental Recovery Plan; new NHS service obligations for newly qualified dentists.
- Women’s health strategy; implement Cass Review (ban puberty blockers privately); protect single‑sex care and language.

Law, order and borders
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; facial recognition, hotspot policing; tougher sentences for violent/sexual/domestic crimes; expand prisons to 20,000 new places by 2030.
- Illegal migration: monthly Rwanda flights; enact Illegal Migration Act; speed asylum to six months; more returns deals; international reform of asylum rules.
- Legal migration: binding annual cap on work/family visas voted by Parliament; higher salary thresholds; pre‑travel health checks; higher fees/IHS.

Energy, climate and environment
- Keep net zero 2050 with “pragmatic” path: annual North Sea licensing; new gas plants for security; treble offshore wind; CCS clusters; accelerate nuclear incl. SMRs; no new green levies or road pricing; bills measures and home efficiency vouchers.
- Protect best farmland from solar; retain fracking moratorium.
- Water plan: tougher penalties/bonus bans; invest fines in river recovery; reform water price reviews.
- Nature: new National Park; tree/peat funding; expand access to green space (no universal Right to Roam); crack down on waste crime; limit new incinerators; ocean protections.

Housing and communities
- Build 1.6m homes: brownfield fast‑track, higher city densities, scrap nutrient neutrality (with mitigation fees); urban development corporations.
- Help to Buy relaunch; permanent FTB Stamp Duty threshold £425k; renters’ reform (end Section 21 with court changes); complete leasehold reform; 2‑year CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants.
- Levelling up: town endowments, Community Ownership Fund, more Freeports/Investment Zones; extend UK Shared Prosperity Fund.

Culture, sport, transport, drivers
- Independent Football Regulator; invest in grassroots sport, women’s sport priority.
- Backing Drivers Bill: ban local road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; require referendums for new LTNs/20mph zones; extend £2 bus fare cap for next Parliament; rail reform creating Great British Railways.

Union, defence and foreign policy
- Defence to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; boost munitions, R&D and procurement reform; strong support to Ukraine and Trident.
- Strengthen UK internal market; continue direct local investment in Scotland, Wales, NI; implement Windsor Framework; Veterans’ Bill and protections.

Sex and gender
- Clarify Equality Act: sex means biological sex; protect single‑sex spaces/sport; one legal sex across the UK; legislate for school guidance on gender-questioning students and parental rights.
